findMatchingSocks.name: Find Matching Socks
findMatchingSocks.description: Write a function that takes two baskets of clothes (as lists of strings) and returns a list of all the pairs of socks found across both baskets. Items that are socks end with ' sock' and always start with 'left ' or 'right '.

solveTightly.name: Solve it in 29 lines
solveTightly.description: Try and solve this in 29 lines of code or fewer. That's not the shortest possible answer, but it's a good target to push towards once you have it working.

oneInEach.name: One in each
oneInEach.description: There's a matching sock in each basket.

aBigMix.name: A big mix!
aBigMix.description: A mix of clothes with multiple matching pairs.

bonusLineCount.name: A tight solution
bonusLineCount.description: The same job, done in fewer lines.

whereToStart.question: Where should I start when there are lots of moving parts?
whereToStart.answer: Don't try to write the whole thing in one go. Break the problem into small functions that each answer one tiny question, get each one working on its own, then combine them.

isItASock.question: How do I tell if something in the basket is actually a sock?
isItASock.answer: Not everything that mentions a side is a sock, and not everything that looks sock-ish is one. Look carefully at the rules for how items are described, and check both ends of the description rather than just the start.

compareSockPair.question: How do I compare a left sock to its right pair?
compareSockPair.answer: Rather than comparing two socks directly, work out what the partner of a sock would be called, then go looking for that. Strings have a built-in method for swapping one piece of text for another, which can also strip a piece off by swapping it for nothing.

avoidDuplicates.question: How do I avoid counting the same pair twice?
avoidDuplicates.answer: Every pair gets discovered twice, once from each side. Before adding a name to your results, check whether it's already in there.

overallPlan.question: What's a good overall plan?
overallPlan.answer: Both baskets can be treated as one big pile. Go through it one item at a time, and for each item decide whether it belongs in your answer.

checks.tooManyLines: So close! Your solution works, but it's more than 29 lines of code.
